company: Racura Oncology Ltd (formerly Race Oncology Limited)
title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Applicable Personnel
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel, Employees and Applicable Consultants (and their employees/officers), collectively 'Applicable Personnel'. All substantive prohibitions, approval and notification requirements in this policy apply uniformly to this group.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: Distinguished only for the approval route: rather than seeking the Chairman's approval, the Chairman must obtain prior approval of the Board before dealing.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Distinguished only for the ASX Listing Rule disclosure obligation: a dealing (personally or through an Associate) that changes a Director's relevant interest must be notified to ASX within 5 business days, and each Director must promptly disclose the required information to the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates such as family members, family trusts and family companies through whom Applicable Personnel deal; the insider trading prohibition and this Policy extend to dealing done through them.

definitions.hedging_definition: must not enter into an agreement with anyone if that arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration without approval of the Company

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's Annual Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's Annual Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Half Year Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Half Year Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's quarterly reports

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion vary the application of a Closed Period by general announcement to Applicable Personnel before or during the Closed Period; not stated to be confidential and no separate officer is given power to impose additional blackouts beyond the fixed Closed Periods.

rules.detail: Trading in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities is expressly named and prohibited only during Closed Periods and without prior Board/Chairman approval; outside those constraints it is permitted with approval. No venue limitation is stated.
rules.evidence: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from trading: (a) during Closed Periods; and (b) without approval of the Company (pursuant to clause 5.1), in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Any arrangement that limits exposure to risk relating to an element of remuneration (which would include equity incentive awards, vested or unvested) requires Company approval; the clause is not expressly limited to unvested holdings.
rules.evidence: Applicable Personnel must not enter into an agreement with anyone if that arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the member's remuneration without approval of the Company.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is a financial product in respect of the Company's securities (caught by 3.6) and/or dealing 'in relation to' securities under 5.1, so it requires prior written approval like any other dealing or derivative.
rules.evidence: Any Applicable Personnel ... wishing to buy, sell, lend, borrow, enter into a secured financing arrangement or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities or derivatives must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman of the Board or the Board before doing so.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. Any sale requires prior written approval under the general approval requirement, which would capture a short sale, but the concept itself is unaddressed.
rules.evidence: Any Applicable Personnel ... wishing to buy, sell, lend, borrow, enter into a secured financing arrangement or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities or derivatives must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman of the Board or the Board before doing so.

rules.detail: Lending or borrowing of the Company's securities is expressly named and prohibited only in the absence of Company approval.
rules.evidence: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from entering into lending (including margin lending), borrowing or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities, without approval of the Company (pursuant to clause 5.1).

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD referencing the Company's securities is a financial product issued or created in respect of those securities, so it is caught by the derivatives clause and requires approval, subject to Closed Periods.
rules.evidence: in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Margin lending is expressly named as a form of prohibited lending/borrowing/secured financing unless approved by the Company.
rules.evidence: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from entering into lending (including margin lending), borrowing or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities, without approval of the Company (pursuant to clause 5.1).

rules.detail: Granting security over the Company's securities is inherent in a 'secured financing arrangement', which is expressly named and listed among the dealings in 5.1 requiring prior written Board/Chairman approval.
rules.evidence: enter into a secured financing arrangement ... in relation to the Company's securities or derivatives must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman of the Board or the Board before doing so.

rules.detail: Secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities are expressly named and permitted only with prior written approval of the Chairman of the Board (or the Board, for the Chairman); there is no outright ban and no tier or vesting carve-out.
rules.evidence: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from entering into lending (including margin lending), borrowing or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities, without approval of the Company (pursuant to clause 5.1).

rules.detail: Aspirational ('should never') rather than absolute prohibition on short-term trading, with a carve-out for exercising options and promptly selling the resulting shares. No defined holding period.
rules.evidence: Applicable Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.approver: Chairman of the Board or the Board
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (written notification of transaction details)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two (2) business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Applicable Personnel (other than the Chairman of the Board) wishing to buy, sell, lend, borrow, enter into a secured financing arrangement or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities or derivatives must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman of the Board or the Board before doing so.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (written notification of transaction details)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two (2) business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chairman of the Board wishes to buy, sell, lend, borrow, enter into a secured financing arrangement or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities or derivatives, the Chairman of the Board must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Applicable Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules)
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board

exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise of the option or right ... falls during a prohibited period
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or in his/her absence, the Chairman of the Board); if the applicant is the Managing Director, all other members of the Board
exceptions.evidence: Applicable Personnel who are not in possession of inside information ... may be given prior written clearance by the Managing Director ... to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities in a Closed Period where the person is in severe financial hardship or where there are exceptional circumstances

exceptions.approver: Managing Director (or in his/her absence, the Chairman of the Board); if the applicant is the Managing Director, all other members of the Board
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company securities or derivatives by an Applicable Personnel if the person is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking ... to transfer or sell securities of the Company, or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.

financing_disclosure: Applicable Personnel: notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of any secured financing arrangement, lending or borrowing (like any other dealing) within two (2) business days of the transaction occurring.

exemption_authority: The Managing Director (or, in his/her absence, the Chairman of the Board) may grant written exemption from Closed Period restrictions for severe financial hardship or exceptional circumstances (e.g. court order or overriding legal/regulatory requirement); where the applicant is the Managing Director, all other Board members decide. Any exemption is in writing and specifies the time period during which the sale may occur. The Company may also vary the application of a Closed Period generally by announcement to Applicable Personnel.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from entering into lending (including margin lending), borrowing or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities, without approval of the Company (pursuant to clause 5.1).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike an outright ban, the loan leg of a funded collar secured on the collared shares is structurally available here provided the Chairman/Board approves it, is entered outside a Closed Period, and the executive holds no inside information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from trading ... during Closed Periods; and ... without approval of the Company ... in financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs of an OTC collar are expressly dealt with as approvable financial products rather than banned outright, so both legs and the loan can in principle be approved together as one transaction.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Applicable Personnel must not, except in exceptional circumstances, deal in securities or derivatives of the Company during the following periods ...
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Closed Period ban expressly extends to derivatives, and the financial-hardship/exceptional-circumstances exemption in 5.5-5.8 is worded only for 'sell or otherwise dispose' of securities, so it is unclear whether an exemption route exists to enter or unwind a collar (as opposed to a share sale) inside a Closed Period; entry/unwind should be scheduled in an open window to avoid the point being tested.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (i.e. a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by an Applicable Personnel needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Physical settlement or a lender's sale on default that exceeds 10% of 20-day ADV triggers a mandatory prior discussion with the Board and legal advisers, which should be factored into unwind/settlement mechanics and timing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no financing carve-out for closed period forced sale
bespoke_clauses.clause: Applicable Personnel are prohibited from entering into lending (including margin lending), borrowing or other secured financing arrangements in respect of the Company's securities, without approval of the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy is silent on what happens if a lender needs to force a sale during a Closed Period (e.g. on a margin call or collar breach); this is a gap the bank's facility documentation should address contractually since the policy gives no exemption route for a third party's enforcement sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Company may at its discretion vary this rule in relation to a particular Closed Period by general announcement to Applicable Personnel either before or during the Closed Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Trading windows for collar entry, adjustment or unwind are not fixed with certainty and can be varied by Company announcement, adding scheduling risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if any Applicable Personnel is in possession of price sensitive information which is not generally available to the market, then he or she must not deal in the Company's securities at any time it is in possession of such information
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval to enter or unwind the collar can be granted but becomes unusable if the executive holds undisclosed price-sensitive information at the intended execution time, regardless of window or clearance status.

summary: A funded collar appears structurally possible under this policy, which is unusually permissive compared to an outright ban: both the derivative legs (put and call, expressly covered as 'financial products issued or created over or in respect of the Company's securities') and the secured loan (an expressly named 'secured financing arrangement') require only prior written approval from the Chairman of the Board (or the Board, if the dealer is the Chairman), rather than being prohibited outright. Execution must occur outside the three Closed Periods (two weeks before to 48 hours after annual, half-year and quarterly reports), the executive must not hold undisclosed price-sensitive information, and the transaction must be notified in writing to the Company Secretary within two business days. There is no defined validity period for an approval and no stated ability to attach conditions, so these should be clarified with the Company Secretary before execution. A sale on unwind or lender enforcement exceeding 10% of 20-day average daily volume requires prior Board and legal-adviser discussion, and the policy is silent on whether a lender's forced sale during a Closed Period is excused, so that risk should be addressed contractually. Overall, subject to case-by-case Board/Chairman approval and careful timing around Closed Periods, a funded collar secured on vested shares is not structurally prohibited.
